alerts.name: posgresql读取时间过高
alerts.note: 数据库中花费在读取文件的时间，这个值很高说明内存较小，需要频繁从磁盘读入数据文件
alerts.note_en: Time spent reading data files. A high value means memory is insufficient and data files are frequently read from disk
alerts.action:
1) 先确认 SHOW track_io_timing 为 on，否则该指标恒为 0，需先开启才有意义；
2) 用 pg_stat_statements 按 shared_blks_read 排序找出读盘最多的 SQL，补索引或改写；
3) 对比 shared_buffers 与实例内存，通常设为物理内存的 25% 左右；
4) 用 iostat -x 1 确认数据目录所在磁盘是否已经打满。

alerts.name: Postgresql down
alerts.action:
1) 登录主机用 systemctl status postgresql 或 docker ps 确认进程是否存活；
2) 进程存活则用 psql -h <host> -p <port> -U <user> 手工连一次，区分实例夯住与网络/pg_hba 认证问题；
3) 进程不在则看 $PGDATA/log 下的日志尾部定位原因（OOM、磁盘满、WAL 目录写满）再拉起；
4) 有流复制备库的立即评估是否需要提升备库（pg_ctl promote）。

alerts.name: postgresql写入时间过高
alerts.note: 数据库中花费在写数据文件的时间，pg中脏页一般写入page cache，如果这个值较高，则说明cache较小，操作系统的cache需要更积极的写入
alerts.note_en: Time spent writing data files. In PG dirty pages are normally written to the page cache; a high value means the cache is small and the OS cache has to flush more aggressively
alerts.action:
1) 先确认 SHOW track_io_timing 为 on，否则该指标恒为 0；
2) 看 pg_stat_bgwriter 的 buffers_backend 是否远大于 buffers_checkpoint——若是说明 shared_buffers 偏小或 bgwriter 太保守；
3) 适当调大 checkpoint_timeout 与 checkpoint_completion_target，把刷盘摊平避免 IO 尖峰；
4) 用 iostat -x 1 确认磁盘是否已打满，必要时换更快的存储。

alerts.name: postgresql有死锁
alerts.action:
1) 在 postgresql.conf 里确认 log_lock_waits=on、deadlock_timeout 合理，然后从日志里取死锁双方的完整 SQL；
2) 查 pg_locks 与 pg_stat_activity 关联，确认是哪两张表、哪种锁互相等待；
3) 根因通常是不同事务以相反顺序更新同几行——统一业务侧的加锁顺序即可消除；
4) 长事务会放大死锁概率，检查是否有事务开启后长时间不提交。

alerts.name: Postgresql缓存命中率低于50%
alerts.action:
1) 先排除刚重启导致的缓存冷启动（对照实例 uptime）；
2) 用 pg_stat_statements 按 shared_blks_read 排序找出读盘最多的 SQL，优先补索引消除全表扫描；
3) 对比 shared_buffers 与实例内存，通常调到物理内存的 25%；
4) 确认是否有大表全量扫描或批处理任务把缓存冲掉，可错峰执行。

collect.content:
# Read metrics from one or many postgresql servers
# # collect interval
# interval = 15

[[instances]]
  ## specify address via a url matching:
  ##   postgres://[pqgotest[:password]]@localhost[/dbname]?sslmode=[disable|verify-ca|verify-full]
  ## or a simple string:
  ##   host=localhost user=pqgotest password=... sslmode=... dbname=app_production
  ##
  ## All connection parameters are optional.
  ##
  ## Without the dbname parameter, the driver will default to a database
  ## with the same name as the user. This dbname is just for instantiating a
  ## connection with the server and doesn't restrict the databases we are trying
  ## to grab metrics for.
  ##
  # address = "host=localhost user=postgres sslmode=disable"

  ## A custom name for the database that will be used as the "server" tag in the
  ## measurement output. If not specified, a default one generated from
  ## the connection address is used.
  # outputaddress = "db01"

  ## connection configuration.
  ## maxlifetime - specify the maximum lifetime of a connection.
  ## default is forever (0s)
  # max_lifetime = "0s"

  ## A  list of databases to explicitly ignore.  If not specified, metrics for all
  ## databases are gathered.  Do NOT use with the 'databases' option.
  # ignored_databases = ["postgres", "template0", "template1"]

  ## A list of databases to pull metrics about. If not specified, metrics for all
  ## databases are gathered.  Do NOT use with the 'ignored_databases' option.
  # databases = ["app_production", "testing"]

  ## Whether to use prepared statements when connecting to the database.
  ## This should be set to false when connecting through a PgBouncer instance
  ## with pool_mode set to transaction.
  #prepared_statements = true
  # [[instances.metrics]]
  # measurement = "sessions"
  # label_fields = [ "state" ]
  # metric_fields = [ "value" ]
  # timeout = "3s"
  # request = '''
  # SELECT COALESCE(state, 'unknown') AS state,
  #        COUNT(*)::double precision AS value
  # FROM pg_stat_activity

  # '''
